Report_ID: Number of children requiring supplementary/rescue analgesia during the first 4 hours after surgery
Title: Postoperative Analgesia in Pediatric Patients: Comparative Study among Local Anesthetics, Opioids and Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs
Author: Menezes MS, Gozzani JL
Comment: Counts derived from explicitly stated percentages: 45% of 20 = 9 children in Group D. The 5% figure is stated jointly for groups B, F, M and S (80 patients); applying it to the 60 opioid-arm patients gives 3 events. The exact per-arm split between B, F, M and S is not reported (Figure 2 is an image), so the opioid-arm event count is an approximation of the paper's own pooled percentage. p-value recorded as the stated significance threshold (p < 0.05) for the chi-square test; exact chi-square statistic not reported for this outcome.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group D - rectal diclofenac potassium 1 mg/kg') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: hospital / operating room and postoperative ward
Participant type: children aged 2-12 years, ASA I-III, undergoing lower-limb orthopaedic, urogenital, anal and infraumbilical procedures under general anaesthesia
Outcome measurement: Proportion of patients per group requiring analgesic complementation (Figure 2; percentages stated in text)
Outcome variable: Number of children requiring supplementary/rescue analgesia during the first 4 hours after surgery
additional_group_ns: Group B caudal 0.25% bupivacaine with epinephrine, n=20 — local anaesthetic arm, excluded per synthesis plan (its patients are included in the paper's pooled "5%" statement for groups B, F, M and S)
effect_direction: favours control (more children needed rescue analgesia with diclofenac: 9/20, 45% vs 3/60, 5% in combined caudal opioid arms; RR > 1)

Title: Diclofenac sodium for post-tonsillectomy pain in children
Author: Watters CH, Patterson CC, Mathews HML, Campbell W
Comment: Paper reports only 'NS' (p >= 0.05) for the diclofenac vs pethidine comparison; no exact p-value or effect measure given, so p_value left empty. Statistic_type inferred from Methods ('Chi-squared tests for contingency tables').; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Diclofenac 1 mg/kg IM') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Children aged 5-12 years, ASA grade 1 or 2, undergoing tonsillectomy with or without adenoidectomy or myringotomy
Recruitment source: Hospital admissions for elective paediatric tonsillectomy
Outcome measurement: Count (and percentage) of children per arm who received rescue pethidine postoperatively
additional_group_ns: Control (no intra-operative analgesia) n = 25, 21 (84%) required pethidine post-operatively — excluded per synthesis plan (no-analgesia arm)
effect_direction: favours control slightly / essentially null (diclofenac 13/25, 52% vs pethidine 12/25, 48%; RR ≈ 1.08, not significant)

Report_ID: Number of children requiring rescue/supplementary postoperative analgesia (first dose of paracetamol) on day of operation
Title: A comparison of rectal diclofenac with intramuscular papaveretum or placebo for pain relief following tonsillectomy
Author: Bone ME, Fell D
Comment: p-value reported only as "p < 0.05" (threshold, not exact); diclofenac arm compared against groups B and C jointly in the paper's own test. Neither analgesia group required postoperative papaveretum (0/20 each), so the paracetamol count represents all rescue analgesia.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group A: rectal diclofenac 2 mg/kg intra-operatively') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Children aged 3-13 years undergoing tonsillectomy with or without adenoidectomy
Recruitment source: Paediatric ENT unit, hospital admissions for tonsillectomy
Outcome measurement: Count of patients receiving supplementary analgesia on the day of operation (Table 4), nursing-staff administered at their discretion
Outcome variable: Number of children requiring rescue/supplementary postoperative analgesia (first dose of paracetamol) on day of operation
additional_group_ns: Group C: control, no intra-operative analgesia, n=20 (17 required first dose of paracetamol, 20 required papaveretum) - excluded per synthesis plan (no-analgesia arm)
effect_direction: favours diclofenac (10/20 vs 17/20 with IM papaveretum; RR ≈ 0.59)

Report_ID: Number of children requiring rescue analgesia after surgery
Title: Post-operative pain relief in children following extraction of carious deciduous teeth under general anaesthesia: a comparison of nalbuphine and diclofenac
Author: Littlejohn, Tarling, Flynn, Ordman & Aiken
Comment: No test statistic or exact p-value reported; paper only states the difference "did not reach statistical significance". Rescue analgesia window is the recovery period (approx. 45 min to discharge), shorter than the plan's 24 h window but the longest reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Diclofenac suppositories 12.5 mg to 1-2 mg/kg rectally') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: hospital day-case dental suite and recovery area
Participant type: children (ASA I-II, aged >=3 years) undergoing day-case extraction of carious deciduous teeth
Recruitment source: London Hospital Dental Institute day-case dental outpatients
Outcome measurement: Count of patients given paracetamol suspension as rescue analgesia in recovery
Outcome variable: Number of children requiring rescue analgesia after surgery
additional_group_ns: No-analgesia control arm n=20 (5 patients given rescue analgesia) — excluded per synthesis plan
effect_direction: favours diclofenac (1/19 vs 3/21 with IV nalbuphine; RR ≈ 0.37, not statistically significant)

Report_ID: Number of children requiring additional/rescue analgesics postoperatively (within 24 h)
Title: Rectally administered diclofenac (Voltaren) reduces vomiting compared with opioid (morphine) after strabismus surgery in children
Author: Wennström & Reinsfelt
Comment: Counts reported in prose without a p-value or significance test for this outcome; denominators (25 per group) taken from Methods/Table headers. Two of the five diclofenac-group events were children with pain score 5 who received i.v. morphine as rescue.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rectal diclofenac (Voltaren) 1 mg/kg') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: hospital (day-case surgery, PACU) with 24 h follow-up by telephone at home
Participant type: Children aged 4-16 years, ASA class I-II, undergoing day-case strabismus surgery
Recruitment source: Department of Anaesthesia, Skaraborg Hospital, Skövde, Sweden; consecutive patients May 1999 - January 2001
Outcome measurement: Count of children receiving extra analgesic (i.v. morphine 0.05 mg/kg in morphine group; repeat rectal diclofenac 1 mg/kg after 6 h or i.v. morphine earlier in diclofenac group) besides scheduled acetaminophen
Outcome variable: Number of children requiring additional/rescue analgesics postoperatively (within 24 h)
effect_direction: favours diclofenac (5/25 vs 10/25 with IV morphine; RR = 0.50)
